juce::Value Class Referencefinal

## Detailed Description

Represents a shared variant value.

A [Value](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1Value.html "Represents a shared variant value.") object contains a reference to a var object, and can get and set its value. Listeners can be attached to be told when the value is changed.

The [Value](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1Value.html "Represents a shared variant value.") class is a wrapper around a shared, reference-counted underlying data object - this means that multiple [Value](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1Value.html "Represents a shared variant value.") objects can all refer to the same piece of data, allowing all of them to be notified when any of them changes it.

When you create a [Value](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1Value.html "Represents a shared variant value.") with its default constructor, it acts as a wrapper around a simple var object, but by creating a [Value](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1Value.html "Represents a shared variant value.") that refers to a custom subclass of [ValueSource](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1Value_1_1ValueSource.html "Used internally by the Value class as the base class for its shared value objects."), you can map the [Value](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1Value.html "Represents a shared variant value.") onto any kind of underlying data.

Important note! The [Value](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1Value.html "Represents a shared variant value.") class is not thread-safe! If you're accessing one from multiple threads, then you'll need to use your own synchronisation around any code that accesses it.

juce::Value Class Referencefinal

Detailed Description

Represents a shared variant value.

A Value object contains a reference to a var object, and can get and set its value. Listeners can be attached to be told when the value is changed.

The Value class is a wrapper around a shared, reference-counted underlying data object - this means that multiple Value objects can all refer to the same piece of data, allowing all of them to be notified when any of them changes it.

When you create a Value with its default constructor, it acts as a wrapper around a simple var object, but by creating a Value that refers to a custom subclass of ValueSource, you can map the Value onto any kind of underlying data.

Important note! The Value class is not thread-safe! If you're accessing one from multiple threads, then you'll need to use your own synchronisation around any code that accesses it.
